metadata.phase: Spatial topology, reusable placement primitives, and Unreal map sync
metadata.task: Define concrete example level kinds, baseline level fields, room applicability, and the first-pass Unreal level browser contents.

summary.overview: Phase 58 concrete planning is closed. The user-approved model now defines the shared loadable `level` concept, the first level kinds, the nesting rules for towns, districts, buildings, and rooms, and the initial hybrid Unreal plugin browsing workflow.

completed-work.item: Locked the first concrete level kinds: `region`, `dungeon-floor`, `dungeon-region`, and `transition-level`.
Locked the structural rule that regions and dungeon-regions do not use rooms directly; rooms belong to dungeon floors and to buildings.
Locked the nested authored structure `town -> district -> building -> room` where districts are optional and buildings may contain rooms.
Locked baseline level fields and the first-pass Unreal browser ordering around overview, structure, content, assets, diagnostics, and placement.
Locked the Unreal implementation target to the `plugins/DB_Unreal_DLC_Plugin` submodule and the hybrid browser-first workflow with managed placement deferred to a selective later scope.
Recorded the pragmatic execution rule that Escape the Dungeon may hardcode non-schema details temporarily after generating as much as possible from schema first.

key-decisions.decision: Towns may contain districts before buildings.
Phase-58 Unreal work targets the DB Unreal DLC Plugin submodule.
Escape the Dungeon stays pragmatic and may hardcode details outside the schema when useful.
The concrete authored world model and Unreal browser baseline are approved.

followups.item: Use this approved model as the baseline for later schema and codegen execution work.
Carry the same nouns into phase 49-style visual planning so topology and editor visuals stay aligned.
Avoid reintroducing unapproved neutral spatial nouns unless they are clearly implementation-only and explicitly documented as such.
